lines.text: Bramblehog first, then the Skir. Then Old Nib.
The notice on the door still says four, and it has since the bad winter.

The Bramblehog's hand-reared off my own line and never learned to keep off a person, so she comes in low and leans. Old Nib is twelve and won't chase you. Whatever's in front of her comes to her, and it comes off that pelt.
Badge is in the apron. Hold on. There.

Old Nib's feet want doing tonight and she won't stand for it on her own, so I'll be an hour in that shed. If you're about at the turn of the year the whole green goes up in lanterns and we feed everybody who walks in.
Old Nib's still on her feet, so she'll not come in off the yard tonight. She does that. Feed her out there and leave her be until morning.
Meadow Reach has gone thin on Nibbin. Mine are penned and hand-fed, so I've the same ones I had in spring.
The Skir come in over my hedge three and four at a time. They only do that when the Reach is short. I put a bucket out at the gatepost for them and they'll take it out of my hand.
I'm in and out of the shed all morning, so speak up.

One of the Bramblehog's off her food. Mouth open, feet up, sound at both ends. The other got through the hedge into the barley and went for the Loamunder in it, so I'm on the barley this morning and the hedge after.
Hold on. — That boat's coming in wrong on the far stilts.
Right. Bogling first, then Reedrick. Whose boat is that.
We go on the slack and not before. Twenty minutes yet, maybe more. Sit down, that bench is Sel's and it holds. Fenmaw comes out last. She's the big one and she takes her time coming up.
Good fight. — The small ones now. Bogling, we call them at that size. They eat the same Reedrick the big ones eat, only smaller ones, and I've had the one animal in my hands at both sizes.
Badge is in the tin by the door. Sel's poling this hour if you want the far bank.
I'm out on the water till the light goes. The slack brings me in and not before it, and I'll be at the stilts when it does.
Brackmarsh has gone quiet on Mirefin. Hold on. The ebb's starting.
The fishery pays less when the marsh is short, so the men on the stilts are on a bad week's money. Hetty has the shallows figure. Hers is better than mine.
The far bank's moved out since the spring. A foot, maybe two.

There's more Sporantle in this marsh than anything else and no buyer for any of them. They sit up against the reed edge and don't shift about. You'll take one out of the same yard of water two days running.
Halder wants three Webvern out of the Wilds canopy, full-grown, and his buyers are contracted.
Eight in that canopy. From the ground, with a glass, the last week of summer, walked by me.

His order is a real one and I have said so at the council table. The old Webvern is last off my bench and she will get her toxin into whatever is standing when she comes out. Whatever happens here goes up dated in the morning.
The old Webvern got her toxin into you. It hardly shows at the first exchange.
It builds. By the sixth it is taking a real piece out of whatever is standing, and there is no shaking it off once it is in. Badge is yours, and all of this goes up written and dated before morning.
The old Webvern gets her strike in the moment she comes out, however quick your animal is. After that she is on her own speed, but the first one is usually enough.
The Barkhide browse the understory back hard, and where they stop it closes over inside two summers. The light down here is on their account.
Halder pins his order up on the market board. My own figure goes up beside it, with the date on it.
Ashvole. Cragmar. Stonewing. Pyrelisk. Then the other Ashvole. No. The warm one's second, she comes out after the first.
Six on the bench. Take as long as you want, and take your coat off first.
Last one's a Pyrelisk as well. Older. Off the west vents. Two seasons, that one took.
Most of that bench goes out the moment it gets wet. The Stonewing doesn't. Half wind, that one. Bram's through the back, past the slag heap.
Here. Your badge. He takes relics gone brittle, not cracked.
Bench is still warm and I'm not banking it down yet. My forge is the small one, thirty feet that way. Give the door a good bang. A soft knock won't carry over the work.
Gerta's at the head of the third shaft most days. Colder up there than down here.
Take a coat up. Ground's warm under the west path, warm since the last flare, and my cellar's warm off the same seam. Nine years of that and the walls in there are dry to the touch.
The room's dark and it stays dark. Bring a lamp for the walk down.
They go out in the order they wake. Last one's a Duskstalk.
Anything of mine can stop an animal where it stands. The woman who had this gym before me left that Duskstalk behind when she went, and I have fed her since.
You got through the Duskstalk. Three have done that before you. Two of the three still come up here in the winter.
Badge. — The gate on to the Approach is off the vale road, a mile past the last light.
The room is the same at noon as it is now. Same dark, and they wake in the same order. The door's not locked.
Dark at four here in the winter, and earlier under the rim.
The Carricrow came into the vale a few years back and stayed. They settle where things have died. The children up here feed them bread out of their hands.
